name: Assembly judged part by part
problem: An assembled system is judged part by part, so nobody checks that it behaves like one capable assistant from where the user sits: asked for something real, it should know what it may do, ask before anything irreversible and say truthfully what it did.
who_has_it: People who use an AI built from many parts, and the teams that assemble it.
why_it_matters: Each part can pass its own test while the whole forgets a promise, acts without asking or reports work it did not do, and the user is the one who finds out.
why_hard: The user's seat spans every part, so no single part's metric sees the failure, and a fair score needs both a measure of overall capability and hard floors on consent and honesty.
existing_attempts: Per-part benchmarks, and hand-run demos of an assistant with no recorded floor for consent or honesty.
